interpretation_notes: What the read licenses: the registered combined read is INCOMPLETE. The 4B lane has no completed, non-void receipt, and the registration allows no amendment under this id. No base, no K1 v3 design (NEGATIVE_CAPABLE_V3 or GO_ONLY_V3) and no stop (NO_K1_V3) is read. In particular it does not license saying that Q3's K1 line stopped for insufficient dense headroom, because that requires both lanes. This holds whatever the summariser defect: the registration's own INCOMPLETE rule decides it.

Claim level, per the Purpose section: this is measurement-only on the development partition (20 passage clusters, 20 questions). It is not a K1 result, positive or negative. It says nothing about whether an indexer loses more cross-script recall than its target. Dense headroom is at most a pre-result about which K1 v3 designs are feasible, never a localization finding.

The 0.6B receipt is valid evidence under every registered void rule; I checked each one. Its per-lane decisions are registered statistics but not the experiment's read. Its lane_class NOT_VIABLE is driven by H2, not H1: H1_CX is 12.25, at least 10, so the lane would have been GO_ONLY_CAPABLE had h2_status not been FAIL. A NEGATIVE-capable design on 0.6B looks excluded (the H1_CX 99% upper bound of 15.59 is below 20). That is a descriptive statement, not a combined-read verdict.

H2 reflects the base model's limited ability, not retrieval. CX multiple-choice accuracy is 31.4 (99% interval 17.1 to 46.4, which includes the 25% chance level). Needle-absent accuracy (35.4) is higher than needle-present, and accuracy with no haystack, the passage alone, is only 36.4. MN accuracy is 49.6. Qwen3-0.6B-Base barely reads cross-script Belebele even when given the passage directly.

Surprising: per-pair headroom collapses when the needle is in a high-fertility language (5 to 6 times English token length). ka>en has CX 0.27 and MN 2.07; ta>en has 1.39 and 3.50; bn>en 3.05 and 5.53; el>en 3.46 and 5.59. English-needle pairs have MN 29.6 and CX 11.9 to 22.7. Even same-language (MN) headroom is near zero for these needles, so the pooled MN minus CX gap (8.55) and H1_CX mostly track needle fertility. The Spearman correlations are -0.82, -0.86 and -0.86, but over only 7 languages, which cannot separate fertility from script or from a language being unseen. This is D26's collinearity in practice.

lexical_confound, entity_control and null_calibration are all NOT_EVALUABLE because of one pair. ka>en's CX target headroom (0.27) is at or below the 1-point evaluability rule, which voids xi_rel on all families for every selector and every sigma. The NOT_EVALUABLE verdicts are therefore structural, not evidence that a confound is present or absent. The one evaluable literal reading, LEX xi_rel on controlled families for target mp, is 0.357, above the 0.10 limit. It hints that lexical overlap persists after entity control (descriptive, one target only).

floor_candidate NOT_VIABLE rests on very lopsided intervals. The near-exact null at sigma 0.25 has a G(MN) point of 0.987 but a 99% lower bound of 0.529. The only V1-adequate sigma that reaches the 2.5-point loss is 0.7 (loss 3.53); its point is 0.905 and its lower bound 0.489, just under 0.5. The lower tail most likely comes from low-headroom pairs hitting the 1-point denominator floor in bootstrap replicates. So NOT_VIABLE reflects how unstable G is on this pair set more than a poor noisy copy. Design decision 10 predicted NOT_VIABLE as the likely outcome.

The block-score null is not exactly centred. Language-agnostic noise gives a negative xi that grows with sigma: -0.05 at 0.25, -0.46 at 0.7 (99% interval -0.85 to -0.07, excluding 0), -0.93 at 1 and -5.5 at 4. The noise costs MN more than CX. The magnitude stays within the 2-point limit at the V1-adequate sigmas (0.25 to 0.7). This measures the identification refuter's concern on real score shapes: the effect is small at realistic noise but not zero.

The 4B lane cannot fit as coded. It ran about 3.8 s per stage-A unit against 0.30 s on 0.6B, about 12.7 times slower, with the GPU idle and one CPU core busy. Scaling 0.6B's per-stage times by that factor puts the full lane at about 55 to 60 minutes (about 1 GPU-h). That is a rough extrapolation, but it exceeds D26's whole 0.5 GPU-h ceiling, not just the 21-minute lane, so any successor needs the CPU-bound path fixed or a new budget decision by the program owner.

The ignored SIGUSR1 made no difference to the outcome. Even a confirmed checkpoint would have left -1 of 21 minutes (charged 22), and the filler refuses a continuation below 5 minutes; the registration states that a time-limit interrupt leaves no room for one. It still matters for a successor's robustness: USR1 was not seen at the chunk boundaries at 04:48:19 and 04:49:23.

Minor: the read had 20 passage clusters, not the 'about 19' in the registration, and half the questions are entity-anchored (Wilson 95% 0.30 to 0.70), so the 30% unanchored precondition of entity_control is met on its point estimate. The operator's deviations (doctor run on the source baked into the image, 4B submitted after the defect was found, charged-basis ledger, entity-anchor words committed, state.json edits) are disclosed. None breaks a registered rule. Running the doctor from the baked source is, if anything, closer to freeze step 3 than mounting a worktree would be.
